  against this exact node, and v10.9 later showed this same node's
  hang was actually inside hostname resolution the whole time - so
  v10.8 may have been solving a problem this port never separately had.
* Reverted to plain blocking connect() on AMIGA - removed all of
  v10.8's and v10.10's non-blocking-socket machinery from client.c,
  back to the same fully-synchronous call this port used successfully
  for months before v10.8 ever touched this file. A genuinely
  unresponsive remote is now bounded only by the host's own underlying
  TCP stack timeout (real and finite, just not configurable from
  AmiBinkD's side anymore) rather than anything AMIGA-specific.
* connect-timeout has no effect on AMIGA as of this release. Left set
  in all 8 deployed .cfg files as a harmless no-op rather than removed,
  in case a future toolchain/emulator fix makes it meaningful again.
* Not yet confirmed against a real successful connection to
  hub.bottomlessabyss.net - this is now the fourth attempt at this
  specific bug across v10.8/v10.9/v10.10/v10.11. Watch the next
  scheduled amiganet poll.

v10.10 - Connect-Completion Detection Fixed (No More select() For This)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

* v10.8's connect-timeout fix used select()/WaitSelect() to detect when
  a non-blocking connect() finished. This is the first release where
  that code got exercised against a real, reachable remote (every
  earlier attempt in this whole investigation got blocked by hostname
  resolution first - see v10.9) - and it hung. Confirmed live: a real
  connection to a hub completed at the TCP level (host-side socket
  state showed CLOSE-WAIT with unread data in the receive buffer - the
  remote had already replied and hung up) but the select() call in
  client.c never returned, hanging the process well past
  connect-timeout with no "connected" or failure line ever logged.
* Same underlying platform limitation as v10.9's UDP finding, a
  different symptom of it: "check writability on a socket that's still
  connecting" is a far less exercised use of WaitSelect() on
  bsdsocket_emu than "check writability on an already-established,
  data-ready socket," which is the only case this whole project has
  actually soak-tested for months (every send()/recv() timeout in
  protocol.c's main loop uses the latter).
* Fixed by not using select()/WaitSelect() for this at all: poll by
  re-issuing connect() on the same non-blocking socket roughly once a
  second (EALREADY = still pending, EISCONN or a 0 return = succeeded,
  anything else = a real failure) via Delay() - the same polling
  primitive amiga/sem.c's _WaitSem() already uses successfully
  elsewhere in this port. The timeout bound comes from AmiBinkD's own
  counter, not from trusting the emulator to honor a select() timeout -
  so even if this specific fix's own assumptions turn out imperfect,
  it still fails safe (bounded, not an indefinite hang).
* Deployed to DH0:AmiBinkd/AmiBinkd (v10.9 kept as
  AmiBinkd.v10.9-backup). Not yet confirmed against a real successful
  connection to hub.bottomlessabyss.net specifically (the case that
  exposed this) - watch for a clean "connected" line on the next
  scheduled amiganet poll.

v10.9 - Host-Resolved DNS Cache (gethostbyname() Never Called On AMIGA)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

* v10.8 fixed connect() having no timeout on AMIGA, but a separate,
  more severe hang remained: polling a hostname-configured hub could
  hang forever *before* connect() was ever reached - inside hostname
  resolution itself. Confirmed live: a poll to a real, reachable hub
  (resolvable instantly from the host machine) sat wedged for 20+
  minutes with zero log output, never even reaching the "trying host
  [ip]..." line that's logged right before connect().
* Root cause: gethostbyname()/gethostbyaddr() (real bsdsocket.library
  calls behind rfc2553.c's getaddrinfo()/getnameinfo() emulation) are
  synchronous, non-cancellable, and non-reentrant (hence the existing
  resolvsem guard around every call). Two seemingly-safer fixes were
  investigated and empirically ruled out, not just reasoned away:
  - Spawn a helper process, abandon it on timeout: the helper still
    needs the same shared resolvsem. If the lookup itself is what's
    stuck, walking away leaves that lock permanently held, poisoning
    DNS resolution for the *entire* running instance, not just one
    poll - worse than the original bug.
  - A hand-built DNS-over-UDP resolver (raw non-blocking socket +
    select(), same pattern as v10.8's connect-timeout fix): a
    standalone test program doing nothing but this was built,
    deployed, and run live. It hung twice - once on an aged instance,
    once immediately after a full guest reboot - with zero output
    before the hang, meaning it froze inside OpenLibrary()/
    socket(SOCK_DGRAM) itself, before any network I/O at all. This
    means Amiberry's bsdsocket_emu doesn't reliably support UDP
    sockets, which is very likely the same root cause behind
    gethostbyname()'s own hang (real DNS resolution needs UDP under
    the hood) - both AMIGA-side "fix it with sockets" approaches were
    dead ends on this specific emulator.
* Fixed by moving resolution off the Amiga side entirely. A new
  host-side script (~/amibinkd-dns/refresh.py, run every 15 minutes
  via a systemd --user timer) parses all deployed .cfg files for
  configured hub hostnames, resolves each one using the host's own
  working resolver, and writes the results to a flat cache file,
  DH0:AmiBinkd/dns_cache.txt - visible to the Amiga guest instantly,
  since Amiberry's HardDrives are host directories with no translation
  layer. rfc2553.c's getaddrinfo() (AMIGA build) now checks for a
  numeric address first (inet_addr() - pure local string parsing, zero
  network I/O, unaffected by either hang above), then looks up the
  cache file via plain fopen()/fgets() (the same file I/O this whole
  codebase already relies on everywhere), and NEVER calls
  gethostbyname() under any circumstance. A cache miss (hostname not
  yet resolved, or the file missing) fails cleanly and immediately
  (EAI_NONAME -> the existing bad_try()/retry handling in client.c,
  unchanged) rather than ever hanging.
* A real regression was caught and fixed during design review before
  this shipped: getaddrinfo() is also called elsewhere in this
  codebase with an already-numeric IP string (AI_NUMERICHOST) to turn
  a peer's known address into a sockaddr, on every single session,
  inbound and outbound. A cache-only replacement without the numeric
  short-circuit would have broken that on every connection, since a
  literal IP string would never appear in the hostname cache. The
  numeric-address check above (checked first, before the cache) covers
  this correctly.
* backresolv (reverse/PTR lookups via getnameinfo()'s gethostbyaddr()
  call) is NOT covered by this fix and remains disabled, same as the
  v10.6-era stopgap - it uses the same broken gethostbyname()/
  bsdsocket_emu path, and since it's cosmetic-only (nicer hostnames in
  the log, nothing functional depends on it), it wasn't judged worth
  the same host-side-cache treatment. See "Known Limitations".

v10.8 - Outbound connect() Timeout (connect-timeout Now Works On AMIGA)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

* Stock binkd already has a connect-timeout config keyword, implemented
  via alarm()/SIGALRM to interrupt a blocking connect() call -- but that
  mechanism is gated to HAVE_FORK-without-HAVE_THREADS builds, and
  classic AmigaOS has neither fork() nor alarm()/SIGALRM. AMIGA's
  connect() call in client.c was therefore always a plain blocking call
  with no bound on it at all, regardless of the connect-timeout setting.
* Confirmed live on 2026-07-27: a poll to a genuinely unresponsive hub
  (39:902/0@amiganet) hung inside connect() indefinitely. Because
  v10.5's AMIGA shutdown drain in exitfunc() deliberately never gives up
  on a still-running session (see v10.5's changelog entry -- a
  CreateNewProcTags child has no segment-list of its own, so letting the
  parent exit while one is still running risks a crash), the whole
  process was then stuck for good once something tried to shut it down,
  recoverable only by a full reset.
* Fixed the portable way rather than chasing an AmigaOS alarm()
  equivalent: when connect-timeout is set, the socket is made
  non-blocking before connect() (the same IoctlSocket(FIONBIO)
  setsockopts() already used post-connect everywhere else in this
  codebase) and the wait for it to complete is bounded with select() --
  exactly the same pattern nettimeout already uses to bound in-session
  I/O. This is the standard, OS-agnostic way BSD-socket code implements
  connect timeouts and needs nothing AmigaOS-specific at all.
* connect-timeout defaults to 0 (disabled) in stock binkd, same as every
  other platform, and none of this BBS's per-network .cfg files had it
  set -- so the fix by itself would have done nothing until the setting
  was actually turned on. Added "connect-timeout 60" to all 8 deployed
  configs (AmiBinkd.cfg and all 7 per-network .cfg files) as part of
  this release. The packaged DH4:AmiBinkD/ example config was NOT
  updated (that whole package has been stale at v10.0 since inception --
  see "Not Done Yet").

v10.7 - Peer/Own-Socket Identity Resolution Race Fix
------------------------------------------------------

* v10.5's design notes already flagged errno as a shared, unprotected
  global across concurrently-running sessions (this toolchain's errno,
  via TCPERR()/TCPERRNO -> strerror(errno)/errno, is libnix's plain
  global, not per-Task storage) and judged it low-severity, deferred.
  Confirmed live on 2026-07-26: a burst of 6 near-simultaneous inbound
  connections all hit protocol()'s getpeername() call at once, and every
  one of them logged the nonsensical "getpeername: No error" -- a
  sibling session's own (successful) syscall reset the shared errno to 0
  in the gap between this session's failing getpeername() and the
  Log() call that read it back. All 6 also resolved to "incoming
  session with unknown" as a result (the getpeername() failure path
  skips hostname/IP resolution entirely). The BBS was reset shortly
  after with no further log activity from those sessions -- undiagnosed
  whether that silence was caused by this race or coincidental, but the
  race itself is clearly real and worth closing regardless.
* Fixed by adding a new dedicated semaphore, peernamesem, held around
  getpeername() and getsockname() in protocol.c, each paired tightly
  with its own immediate TCPERR()/errno-dependent logging -- so two
  sessions can no longer interleave between "the syscall runs" and
  "its errno gets logged." A dedicated semaphore rather than reusing
  hostsem/resolvsem, since this code path itself calls into
  getnameinfo() (rfc2553.c), which already takes those internally --
  reusing either here would self-deadlock.
* Scope note: this fixes the specific getpeername()/getsockname()
  critical section that was actually observed racing. Other TCPERR()/
  TCPERRNO call sites elsewhere (client.c's outbound connect()/socket()/
  bind(), server.c's servmgr setup, iptools.c's ioctl paths) have the
  same latent shared-errno exposure but haven't been observed racing in
  practice and are not covered by this release -- see section 16.

v10.6 - Stale .csy/.bsy Hold Actually Honored
------------------------------------------------

* v10.3 added a give-up/backoff to process_bsy(): after
  BSY_GIVEUP_TRIES (3) consecutive failed unlink attempts on a stale
  .csy/.bsy, it would log "giving up ... holding Ns" and call
  hold_node() to mark that address unavailable for BSY_GIVEUP_HOLD
  (300) seconds. What it never did was check that hold before trying
  again itself: process_bsy() re-ran its full stat()/unlink attempt on
  every single directory rescan regardless of an active hold, so the
  "holding 300s" message was cosmetic -- it kept re-attempting (and
  re-failing, and re-logging "giving up ... holding 300s") roughly
  once per rescan_delay the whole time it claimed to be holding.
* Confirmed live on 2026-07-26: a wedged 80:774/0@retronet .bsy lock
  produced over 900 "giving up removing stale .bsy ... holding 300s"
  log lines across a continuous ~4-hour stretch (03:07-07:05), hammering
  the filesystem and log the entire time, before the BBS was manually
  reset. The v10.3 hold_node() call was doing its job for outbound
  dialing (q_next_node() already honors hold_until correctly) -- only
  process_bsy()'s own retry loop was ignoring it.
* Fixed by having process_bsy() check node->hold_until at the very top,
  before doing anything else: if the node is currently held, return
  immediately without stat()-ing the file, attempting an unlink, or
  logging anything. Once the hold naturally expires (already handled by
  the existing process_hld()/.hld-file mechanism), normal handling
  resumes automatically.
* Note: like v10.1 and v10.3, this does not root-cause why the
  underlying lock file sometimes never releases -- it makes the
  existing backoff actually take effect instead of being purely
  cosmetic.

v10.5 - Real Concurrency (CreateNewProcTags)
------------------------------------------------

* Through v10.4, branch.c ran every session (inbound or outbound)
  synchronously - no fork()/pthreads without ixemul.library, which this
  port deliberately avoids. v10.5 adds real concurrency: each session
  now runs as its own genuine AmigaOS process via
  CreateNewProcTags(NP_Entry=...) - see section 05 for the full
  explanation, including why this behaves closer to a thread than a
  Unix fork() on classic AmigaOS's single flat address space.
* NP_Entry takes no startup argument, and this codebase's own
  SIGF_SINGLE turned out to be the same physical bit as SIGF_BLIT
  (graphics.library's blitter signal) - not a safe, documented way to
  hand the child its session data. Used instead: spawn the child one
  NP_Priority below the parent's current priority, then store the args
  pointer in the child's tc_UserData with no synchronization needed -
  AmigaOS's priority-preemptive scheduler guarantees the (lower-
  priority) child cannot run before the (higher-priority, still-ready)
  parent has finished that store.
* bsdsocket.library (Roadshow) denies Processes other than the one that
  opened it access to its functions by default. Every session but the
  very first would have silently failed all socket calls without
  amiga_socket_init() opting into SBTC_CAN_SHARE_LIBRARY_BASES.
* Fixed a latent race in the final n_servers/n_clients decrement
  (server.c's serv(), client.c's call()): a bare, unprotected decrement
  that was only ever safe because branch() never ran two sessions at
  once before now. Wrapped in threadsafe(), matching the HAVE_THREADS
  build's existing equivalent (the semaphore infrastructure itself was
  already fully implemented for AMIGA, just unused until now).
* Fixed qn_free() (ftnq.c) unconditionally clearing every node's
  in-memory busy flag on every outbound-queue rebuild, including nodes
  whose session might now still be genuinely running concurrently. Left
  harmless in practice by call()'s own separate F_CSY disk-lock check
  (a resulting duplicate dial attempt just logs "busy, skipping" rather
  than actually double-dialing), but fixed at the source to avoid the
  wasted attempt and log noise.
* Rewrote exitproc.c's shutdown path for AMIGA: waits indefinitely for
  in-flight sessions to finish rather than timing out after a few
  seconds and proceeding anyway, unlike the HAVE_THREADS build's
  equivalent. This is deliberate, not a lesser implementation - a
  CreateNewProcTags(NP_Entry=...) child has no pr_SegList reference of
  its own to the code it's executing, only the parent's does, so
  letting the parent's exit() complete while a child was still running
  risked the child executing out of memory that had just been freed.
  See section 12's "seems to hang instead of exiting" entry.
* SLEEP() (the scheduler's idle-wait, client.c) now wakes early via
  wakecmgr for AMIGA too, matching HAVE_THREADS - a finished concurrent
  session PostSem()'s it, so a freed session slot gets reused promptly
  instead of waiting out whatever's left of the current poll interval.
* Known, accepted limitations of this first concurrent release (shared
  errno/mypid/rand() state across sessions) are documented in section
  05, not fixed - low practical risk, judged not worth the added
  complexity for this release.

v10.4 - n_servers Leak Fix (Inbound "too many servers")
------------------------------------------------------------

* Confirmed live on 2026-07-25: every inbound connection started failing
  with "too many servers" starting around 11:03PM the previous night,
  including the BBS's own local scheduler triggering scheduled network
  polls (source 192.168.86.1) -- not just outside connections. Outbound
  polling (this BBS dialing out to hubs) was unaffected throughout,
  which is why nothing else looked wrong.
* Root cause: the exact same class of bug as the n_clients leak fixed
  during the original v10.0 port (see section 17, finding 7 / the
  client.c bullet under "What had to change") -- but on the *inbound*
  side, which never got the equivalent fix. server.c's serv() (the
  per-inbound-session worker) increments n_servers unconditionally on
  every accepted connection, but only decrements it under
  HAVE_THREADS or DOS/DEBUGCHILD -- AMIGA was missing from that
  #elif, unlike client.c's call(), which already includes AMIGA in its
  own equivalent decrement. Every inbound session on this port
  therefore leaked n_servers by +1 forever. Once the count exceeded
  max_servers (100, the binkd default -- not overridden in
  AmiBinkd.cfg), every subsequent inbound connection was rejected
  permanently, since the counter never shrinks on its own. Only a
  process restart clears it -- this cannot self-heal.
* Fixed by adding AMIGA to server.c's decrement #elif, mirroring
  client.c's existing pattern exactly: "#elif defined(DOS) ||
  defined(DEBUGCHILD) || defined(AMIGA)". One-line change.
* Note: v10.3's stale-.csy/.bsy give-up/backoff logic (previous
  section) is unrelated to this bug and continues to work as designed
  -- this is a separate, independent leak in a different counter.

v10.3 - Stale .csy/.bsy Give-Up/Backoff
------------------------------------------

* v10.1 made the .csy/.bsy stale-lock unlink retry-capable (sdelete(),
  up to 5 attempts 1 second apart) but that retry loop was itself
  retried forever, once per rescan_delay, by the outer scheduler
  (process_bsy() in ftnq.c) any time the underlying lock never actually
  clears. Confirmed live on 2026-07-23: an ArakNet stale .bsy for
  10:100/0 never cleared, and process_bsy() kept re-attempting the
  unlink every ~5 seconds continuously for over 3 hours (01:40-05:14)
  without ever completing that poll. Because this port runs one BinkP
  session at a time (section 05) and the driver scripts (section 09)
  Execute each network's poll in sequence, this single wedged node
  blocked every other configured network from being polled at all for
  the rest of the night -- not the purely cosmetic failure mode
  documented in v10.1's changelog entry.
* Fixed by giving process_bsy() a bounded number of consecutive
  unlink-failure attempts (BSY_GIVEUP_TRIES, currently 3) per node
  before backing off, rather than retrying immediately forever. Once
  the threshold is hit, it logs a clear "giving up removing stale ...
  after N tries, holding Ns" message and calls the existing hold_node()
  mechanism (already used elsewhere for connection-retry backoff) to
  mark that address unavailable for BSY_GIVEUP_HOLD seconds (currently
  300). q_next_node()/q_not_empty() both already honor hold_until, so
  a held node with nothing else queued lets that invocation cleanly
  log "the queue is empty, quitting" and exit -- letting the driver
  script move on to the next network on schedule instead of hanging.
  The failure counter (FTN_NODE.bsy_fail_count) resets to 0 on any
  successful unlink, so an address that clears its own lock goes right
  back to normal handling.
* Note: like v10.1, this does not root-cause *why* the lock sometimes
  never clears (still suspected to correlate with heavy concurrent
  file-write activity on the same drive image, per the BBS-side
  incident notes) -- it bounds the damage from that condition instead
  of eliminating the condition itself. A node that hits this repeatedly
  will keep cycling through 3 failed tries + a 5-minute hold rather
  than either hanging forever or silently going quiet permanently.

v10.2 - .dt Unlink Message Fix
--------------------------------

* Fixed the rare ("error unlinking '...Inbound_Temp/*.dt': No such file
  or directory") message documented as a cosmetic issue in v10.1's
  "Known Limitations" (section 16).
* Root cause was different from the v10.1 .csy/.bsy fix even though the
  symptom looked similar: remove_hr() (inbound.c) unconditionally tried
  to delete a partial transfer's .dt data file whenever it cleaned up
  the matching .hr semaphore file. The .dt file is only created once
  inb_fopen() actually starts receiving data for that transfer -- if a
  partial/dup/old .hr marker gets cleaned up before any bytes ever
  arrived (e.g. session dropped right after the file was negotiated but
  before the data phase started), there was no .dt file to remove, and
  unlink()'s expected ENOENT got logged as a level-1 error.
* Note this is NOT the same fix as v10.1: swapping delete() for
  sdelete() here would not have helped, since sdelete()'s retry loop
  only retries on EPERM/EACCES/EAGAIN/ETXTBSY (lock-race errnos) and
  still logs on ENOENT. Instead, remove_hr() now stat()s the .dt file
  first and only attempts the delete (and thus only logs) if it
  actually exists -- the same "ENOENT is an expected outcome, don't
  log it as an error" precedent already used for pid-file cleanup in
  binkd.c. Single-session-at-a-time concurrency (section 05) means
  there's no stat-then-delete race to worry about.

v10.1 - .csy/.bsy Unlink Fix
------------------------------

* Fixed the .csy/.bsy busy-flag unlink failure documented as a cosmetic,
  not-yet-root-caused issue in v10.0's "Known Limitations" (section 16).
  bsy_remove()/bsy_remove_all() (bsy.c) and process_bsy()'s stale-file
  cleanup (ftnq.c) were calling delete(), a single-attempt unlink, while
  this codebase already had a retry-capable sdelete() (tools.c) built for
  exactly this class of transient Amiga file-lock race -- bsy.c simply
  never used it. Worse, even sdelete() didn't retry on ETXTBSY ("Text
  file busy"), the specific errno actually being hit.
* sdelete() now also retries on ETXTBSY (up to 5 attempts, 1 second
  apart), matching its existing retry behavior for EPERM/EACCES/EAGAIN.
  bsy_remove(), bsy_remove_all(), and process_bsy() all switched from
  delete() to sdelete().
* Verified live: AmigaNet hit the exact "Text file busy" condition
  post-deploy, visibly retried for ~5 seconds, and completed its session
  normally afterward -- confirming the retry path works without
  introducing any blocking or hangs of its own.
* Note: the underlying transient lock that makes the file briefly
  unremovable is still not root-caused -- this fix makes the cleanup
  attempt robust (and consistent with how the rest of the codebase
  already handles this exact class of race) rather than eliminating the
  brief lock itself. The "error unlinking ... Text file busy" message
  can still appear in logs on occasion; it no longer reflects a
  single-attempt failure with no retry.

v10.0 - Native AmigaOS Port
----------------------------

* Rebuilt from a clean upstream binkd checkout with every ixemul/ixnet
  dependency replaced by native AmigaOS/bsdsocket.library equivalents.
* AMIGA build target now runs each BinkP session synchronously (same
  code path as stock binkd's non-fork/non-thread "DOS" fallback)
  instead of using ixemul's vfork()-based concurrency.
* Found and fixed five real Amiberry bsdsocket_emu behavioral
  divergences from genuine BSD sockets (getaddrinfo()/getnameinfo() not
  implemented, non-blocking-mode ioctl/fcntl not working on sockets,
  accept() not guaranteed non-blocking after a ready select(),
  WaitSelect()'s signals parameter not working, and WaitSelect()
  breaking under rapid repeated calls) -- see section 15.
* Fixed n_clients never being decremented for the AMIGA build target,
  which hung multi-node polling (or chained per-network driver scripts)
  right after the first session completed -- see section 15, finding 7.
* Fixed o_rename()'s inverted success/failure return value and missing
  errno, which silently orphaned received files under their temp names
  in temp-inbound -- see section 15, finding 8.
* Fixed a PRIuMAX/PRIdMAX format-string size mismatch (4-byte format
  specifier against this toolchain's real 8-byte intmax_t/uintmax_t)
  that corrupted outgoing M_FILE protocol message fields on any session
  with real mail queued, causing "missing tmp file" failures on the
  receiving end.
* Cross-compiled clean (zero warnings) with the bebbo/amiga-gcc
  toolchain; confirmed zero ixemul/ixnet references and zero FPU
  instructions in the built binary.
* Verified live on a production Amiberry instance: both outbound
  (client/poll) and inbound (server) sessions, full multi-network
  polling (7 networks) in one run with real inbound file reception and
  successful tosser import, and an unattended overnight soak test
  across all seven networks with no hangs and no regressions.


===============================================================================
19. DISCLAIMER
===============================================================================

AmiBinkD is provided as-is.

This is a from-scratch reconstruction of ixemul-dependent Amiga binkd
behavior, verified against one real system (Amiberry-emulated AmigaOS
3.x, bsdsocket_emu). Other bsdsocket.library implementations (real
Roadshow, AmiTCP) have not been tested and may behave differently --
see section 15 before assuming a finding there applies beyond Amiberry.

Every FTN network and BBS system is different. Test carefully, using
section 11's procedure, before relying on this for live mail.

The author is not responsible for lost mail, misconfigured domains or
addresses, missing or wrong node passwords, or damage caused by
improper setup.

Always keep backups.


===============================================================================
20. CREDITS AND CONTACT
===============================================================================

AmiBinkD is a native AmigaOS port of binkd
(https://github.com/pgul/binkd), originally written by Dima Maloff and
maintained by the binkd project. All BinkP protocol logic, FTN packet
handling, and configuration semantics are upstream binkd's; this port's
own contribution is the AmigaOS/bsdsocket.library integration layer and
the real-hardware fixes documented in section 15.

Earlier Amiga port (AmiBinkd v5.00 - v9.02, 2012-2013):

Rudi Timmermans, X-TReMe BBS

AmiBinkD carried this name on the Amiga long before the present release.
Rudi Timmermans built and maintained it through v9.02, made it freeware
at v5.00, and got a working BinkP mailer onto classic AmigaOS at a time
when that meant living with ixemul.library. This port is a from-scratch
reconstruction rather than a recompile of his -- the ixemul dependency is
gone and every session now runs as a native AmigaOS process (section 05)
-- but the program's name, its configuration file format, and the shape
of its session log all come from his work. Set a v9.01 log from 2013
beside one from this release and they are recognisably the same program.
Credit where it is due.

Built and tested for:

Reign of Fire BBS
C-Net/5 Amiga Pro
call.rofbbs.com:6800

Created for the C-Net/5 SysOp community and other retro BBS operators
who want native FTN mail transport on real or emulated Amiga systems
without an ixemul.library dependency.

Website:

https://www.rofbbs.com

SysOp / Author (Amiga port):

Gary "Spitfire" McCulloch

Networks tested against:

AmigaNet, ArakNet, CommodoreNet, DiscipleNet, FidoNet, PiNet, RetroNet
